recognize_zh: 視野左側有一顆接近紅血球大小、帶紫色顆粒的巨大血小板（giant platelet），旁邊可比對一顆正常小血小板；結合標題即指向 MYH9 相關疾病（May-Hegglin anomaly）。本圖只見嗜酸性球，看不到嗜中性球中的 Döhle-like 包涵體。
features: Giant platelet approaching the diameter of a small red cell, with central purple granulomere and pale hyalomere
Normal-sized platelet nearby for comparison, highlighting platelet size heterogeneity
Central eosinophil with bilobed nucleus and abundant orange-red granules; no neutrophil present to assess for Döhle-like inclusions
Red cells largely normocytic and normochromic without significant poikilocytosis
Overall paucity of platelets in the field, compatible with thrombocytopenia
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic, normochromic red cells with few platelets in the field. A giant platelet approaching red-cell size is present adjacent to an unremarkable eosinophil, with a normal-sized platelet nearby. No neutrophils are present in this field, so the characteristic basophilic Döhle-like cytoplasmic inclusions cannot be evaluated here. In the appropriate context, macrothrombocytopenia is suggestive of an MYH9-related disorder (May-Hegglin anomaly).

ddx.vs: Also shows giant platelets but lacks neutrophil inclusions and has absent ristocetin-induced agglutination due to GPIb-IX-V deficiency.
Large platelets are pale gray and agranular owing to alpha-granule deficiency, whereas this platelet retains purple granules.
Large young platelets may be seen, but truly giant platelets and neutrophil Döhle-like inclusions are absent and MYH9 immunofluorescence is normal.
Reactive Döhle bodies accompany toxic granulation in infection and are not associated with giant platelets.
